paper_metadata.title: Extensive Benchmark of Frugal Encoder–Decoder Language Models for Datatype Properties Extraction and RDF Knowledge Graph Generation
paper_metadata.abstract: The article benchmarks five encoder-decoder pretrained language models—BART, T5, CodeT5, FlanT5, and PileT5—fine-tuned for restricted relation extraction that generates facts from text. It evaluates 13 output linearizations, including RDF standard syntaxes, for triple validity, extraction performance, training behavior, and resource use, and identifies Turtle Light as a quick and robust syntax for learning the task.

problem_addressed: Determine how RDF output linearization affects fine-tuned frugal encoder-decoder models for extracting datatype-property facts from Wikipedia abstracts and directly generating RDF graphs for DBpedia dbo:Person resources. The paper specifically seeks the model/syntax trade-off that maximizes extraction quality and expressivity while minimizing cost.

methodology.description: The method treats restricted relation extraction as supervised sequence-to-sequence translation from a Wikipedia abstract plus the target DBpedia entity URI to a linearized RDF graph. Pipeline order: (1) obtain a DBpedia dump and matching Wikipedia abstracts; (2) select dbo:Person datatype triples; (3) retain graph descriptions valid against a maximal SHACL shape and retain only triples whose values occur in the paired abstract; (4) order triples with rdf:type first and URL-encode/clean URIs; (5) serialize each graph in 13 alternatives—list/tags and factorized versions, RDF/XML, N-Triples, Turtle, JSON-LD, Turtle Light variants, and Turtle Ultra Light—with vocabulary extensions for W3C syntaxes; (6) make cross-validation splits; (7) fine-tune BART, T5, CodeT5, FlanT5, and PileT5 base models using model-specific prompts; (8) parse generated output and measure RDF validity, SHACL validity, subject correctness, extraction quality, learning dynamics, training time, and CO2. Supplementary experiments test EBNF grammar-constrained decoding, CodeT5-based refinement, and robustness to reordered/masked/no-URI/no-instruction prompts. No entity linking, coreference resolution, or joint entity-relation extraction module is described; the supplied entity URI identifies the graph subject.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: A maximal SHACL NodeShape targeting dbo:Person constrains dataset creation, required/optional datatype properties, and validation. It includes rdf:type, rdfs:label, dbo:birthDate or dbo:birthYear, dbo:deathDate, dbo:deathYear, dbo:alias, and dbo:birthName with datatype/cardinality constraints. Outputs are evaluated by their rate of SHACL-valid parsed triples. The shape is a predefined schema constraint, not ontology discovery.

text_to_kg_stages: Text preprocessing: filter DBpedia–Wikipedia pairs by value occurrence in abstracts; order triples; URL-encode and clean URIs; typographically clean prediction/reference outputs
Entity typing: generate rdf:type dbo:Person as part of the output graph
Relation and triple extraction: generate datatype-property RDF triples from Wikipedia abstracts
Graph construction: directly generate linearized RDF graphs/serializations
Graph validation and correction: parse generated triples; measure SHACL validity; supplementary constrained decoding and CodeT5 refinement experiments

input_output.input_type: English Wikipedia abstracts paired with a DBpedia entity URI; training labels are DBpedia graphs containing selected dbo:Person datatype properties.
input_output.input_granularity: One entity-level Wikipedia abstract at a time, with the target entity URI in the input prompt.
input_output.output_representation: A set of RDF triples/graph describing one dbo:Person entity and its datatype properties, generated as one of 13 textual linearizations: list, tags, factorized list/tags, RDF/XML, N-Triples, Turtle, JSON-LD, Turtle Light variants, or Turtle Ultra Light. The target properties are rdf:type, rdfs:label, dbo:birthYear, dbo:birthDate, dbo:deathYear, dbo:deathDate, dbo:birthName, and dbo:alias.

models_and_tools: Fine-tuned base encoder-decoder models: BART (140M parameters), T5 (220M), CodeT5 (220M), FlanT5 (248M), and PileT5 (248M)
Model prompts: BART uses '$entity_URI : $Abstract'; T5-family models use 'Translate English to $Syntax: [$entity_URI] $Abstract'
Code base: open-licensed fork of REBEL, extended for the task; syntax-specific parsers and typographic checker/cleaner
RDFlib for deterministic triple-ordering issue handling; SHACL/ShapeVOWL for target-shape representation; CodeCarbon for CO2-equivalent measurements
Supplementary tools: transformers-CFG extended for BART/T5 EBNF-constrained decoding; pretrained and fine-tuned CodeT5 tested as RDF syntax refiners
datasets: Custom ground-truth dataset D sampled from DBpedia Snapshot 2022-09 and paired Wikipedia abstracts
Scope: 6,000 dbo:Person entities, reported as described by 28M triples; selected target properties have 13,832 distinct values
Data quality processing: retain only DBpedia graphs valid against the maximal SHACL shape and only triples whose values are present in the matched Wikipedia abstract
Evaluation/training split: 5,000 examples in rotating 5-fold cross-validation (4,000 train and 1,000 test per fold), plus 250 disjoint evaluation examples

metrics: Parsed-triples rate RPT = parsed generated outputs / generated outputs
Correct-subject rate RCS = outputs containing the target URI / parsed outputs
SHACL-validated-triples rate RSVT = valid parsed outputs / parsed outputs
Strict micro precision, recall, F1 (F1−) and macro per-property precision, recall, F1 (P+, R+, F1+)
BLEU for similarity of string datatype values; Levenshtein edit distance for non-parsable RDF output
Global grade Gg = RPT × RCS × RSVT × F1+ × 100
Training behavior: velocity, stability, and divergence, monitored for RPT and F1− at saturation threshold 0.9
Resources: training time in minutes and CodeCarbon CO2-equivalent grams
baselines: Within-study comparison across all model–linearization configurations (five encoder-decoder models and 13 syntax variants); the original model M is defined as predicting an SHACL-valid graph from an abstract
Context robustness baselines for BART Bvt1f and T5 T5vt1f: baseline inputs versus reordered sentences, masked entity URI, no entity URI, and (for T5) no instruction
No external state-of-the-art method baseline is reported as evaluated in the main benchmark
evaluation.setting: Controlled supervised benchmark over 13 output syntaxes and five base-size encoder-decoder models. Models are fine-tuned on a single GPU: Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB for BART and NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe for T5-family models. BART uses inverse-square-root scheduling with initial learning rate 0.00005; T5-family models use Adafactor with 0.001. All use 1,000 warm-up steps and early stopping patience 5. The paper states 5-fold data cross-validation, while metric averaging is described as over 10 folds for each configuration; this inconsistency should be checked before using the aggregate results in a final review.

value: Best global-grade configuration: T5 with vocabulary extension and JSON-LD (T5vj): RPT=1.00, RCS=1.00, RSVT=1.00, macro F1+=95.63±8.1, macro precision=100.00, macro recall=94.37, BLEU=1.00, Gg=96; it required 137.362 minutes and 0.252 g CO2-equivalent.

Best reported frugal compromise: BART with vocabulary extension, one-line factorized Turtle Light (Bvt1f): RPT=RCS=RSVT=1.00, macro F1+=94.54±7.3, Gg=95, 26.801 minutes, and 0.035 g CO2-equivalent. The conclusion calls it a good efficiency/frugality trade-off.
BART factorized tags (Bvgf) had macro F1+=95.47±8.1 and Gg=95 with 29.149 minutes/0.042g; BART Turtle Ultra Light (Bvu) had macro F1+=95.25±6.7 and Gg=95 with 42.000 minutes/0.056g.

BART and T5 were the strongest model families; CodeT5 was third despite no Wikipedia pretraining. FlanT5 and PileT5 were unable to solve the task reliably; for Turtle Ultra Light their RPT values were 0.95 and 0.59, respectively.

Output syntax is decisive: Turtle Ultra Light was robust across models, W3C syntaxes were generally poorer, and factorization plus one-line writing improved Turtle Light. Light syntax can greatly reduce output length; for BART, one-line factorized Turtle Light required 121 tokens for the longest 7-property target versus 541 with JSON-LD.

Grammar-constrained decoding was unsuccessful in this setting: about 250 ms/token, roughly six times unconstrained decoding, with incomplete and syntactically invalid output. Fine-tuned CodeT5 partially corrected malformed Turtle Light but reduced triple count and sometimes changed factual values or omitted facts.

Prompt robustness: reordered sentences preserved or slightly improved macro F1+ for Bvt1f (78.22 baseline; 80.23 reordered) and T5vt1f (68.84; 73.67), but removing/masking the entity makes RCS zero; removing T5's instruction reduced macro F1+ to 54.78 and Gg to zero.

value: Author-reported: comprehensive controlled benchmark crossing five relatively small encoder-decoder models with 13 RDF/graph linearizations, assessing validity, extraction quality, training behavior, time, and carbon footprint.
Author-reported: target labels are quality filtered by a maximal SHACL shape and by checking that values occur in the paired Wikipedia abstract, directly addressing distant-supervision mismatch.
Author-reported: uses syntax-aware parsing, subject-copy, SHACL-validity, strict macro property metrics, string BLEU, and resource measures rather than F1 alone.
Author-reported: yields an implementable high-quality/frugal configuration, BART + one-line factorized Turtle Light, with fully parsed, correct-subject, SHACL-valid outputs and Gg 95.

[Review-level inference] The focused, closed dbo:Person datatype-property schema makes the empirical comparison especially useful for choosing serialization and model configurations in similarly constrained RDF population tasks.

value: Author-reported: the task is restricted to datatype properties for dbo:Person and a small fixed target shape; it does not demonstrate general open-domain or object-property graph construction.
Author-reported: models depend on a supplied target entity URI; masking or omitting it yields RCS=0, so they cannot autonomously identify the graph subject.
Author-reported: syntactic correctness remains a bottleneck; malformed outputs can arise from omitted/misplaced syntax tokens, truncation, or empty/incomplete sequences.
Author-reported: constrained grammar decoding was slow and ineffective here; CodeT5 refinement could make syntactic repairs but at the cost of missing facts or corrupted values.

[Review-level inference] Because labels are retained only when DBpedia values are literally found in the abstract and the output schema is constrained, the reported scores should not be interpreted as performance on extracting all facts expressed in unrestricted text.

value: The benchmark is restricted to a predefined maximal SHACL shape for dbo:Person datatype properties; future work is needed to extend it to shapes containing both data and object properties at knowledge-base scale.
The models cannot reliably infer the subject entity URI when it is masked or absent from the prompt.
Constrained decoding with the available library did not work in the experimental setting: it substantially increased inference time and often produced incomplete/invalid output.
Direct pretrained CodeT5 did not understand RDF/Turtle conventions sufficiently to fix simple errors; fine-tuned CodeT5 only partially repaired errors and could alter values or omit information.
The authors note that formal comparison of some metrics is limited where FlanT5/PileT5 configurations never reach saturation.

value: Author-proposed: extend the approach from the restricted dbo:Person datatype shape to knowledge-base-scale shapes that contain both datatype and object properties.
Author-proposed: further fine-tune code-oriented models using explicit refinement examples to improve RDF syntax repair.

Author-proposed/conditional: verify whether grammar-constrained decoding can benefit small language models with a more effective implementation, while addressing its inference cost and complex-grammar failures.

[Review-level inference] Evaluate on multiple entity classes, relations involving entities, and held-out temporal/domain sources to establish transfer beyond the fixed person schema and value-in-text filtering.
[Review-level inference] Add a subject-identification/linking component or evaluate models without a gold entity URI, since subject copying is required for successful RCS.

value: Whether results on this constrained, datatype-only dbo:Person extraction task transfer to knowledge-base-scale RDF generation with object properties and broader shapes.
How to obtain syntactically valid structured output from small encoder-decoder models without costly/ineffective constrained decoding or semantic damage during post-generation correction.
How to infer or link the correct graph subject without providing its entity URI in the input.
How to handle the quality/completeness mismatch between DBpedia triples and text outside the paper's filtering setup.
[Review-level inference] The paper does not resolve coreference, entity linking, or cross-document entity resolution, which would be needed for a complete open-text-to-KG pipeline.
